artists.biography:
John Grant is an American singer-songwriter. He recently launched his career as a solo artist, having previously been lead vocalist with The Czars, an alternative rock band he formed in 1994 in Denver with Chris Pearson. Following the band's breakup, Grant took some time off from making music, and returned to recording and performing in 2010 with his debut solo album Queen of Denmark.
He released Queen of Denmark on April 6, 2010. It was recorded in collaboration with the American folk rock band Midlake, and released on Bella Union. Described as a deeply personal album about his past struggles with alcohol and drug addiction and coming to terms with being gay, it was chosen as Best Album of 2010 by the British music magazine Mojo.

perplexity.description:
Queen of Denmark is the debut solo album by American singer-songwriter John Grant, released on April 19, 2010, through the Bella Union label. After the breakup of his previous band The Czars and a four-year hiatus, Grant was encouraged by the folk rock band Midlake to return to music. The album was recorded in Midlake’s Denton, Texas studio, with members of the band collaborating on production and instrumentation. Musically, it blends rock, folk, country, and world influences, characterized by rich acoustic arrangements, orchestral touches, and subtle synths, all supporting Grant’s deep, expressive baritone voice.

The album marks a significant artistic rebirth for Grant, featuring literate, poetic lyrics that explore themes of alienation, love, and identity with a mix of wry humor and emotional depth. It stands out for its confessional style without succumbing to self-pity, instead offering a dark yet optimistic perspective. Critics widely praised Queen of Denmark for its emotional honesty and sophisticated sound, with Mojo magazine awarding it the rare "Instant Classic" label and naming it the Best Album of 2010. BBC Music called it "one of the most deeply satisfying debut albums of recent times," highlighting its blend of sad yet hopeful love songs and elegant arrangements.

Commercially, while not a mainstream blockbuster, the album established John Grant as a distinctive solo artist with a devoted following and critical acclaim. It remains a cornerstone of his discography, setting the tone for his subsequent releases and solidifying his reputation for combining sharp lyricism with lush, genre-spanning music.
